finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied `f` parameter is joined onto /srv/files with no check that the result stays under the root. filepath.Join cleans `..` segments, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd and is served. Any unauthenticated client can read arbitrary files readable by the server process.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)), with the contents written to the response

trace.note: /dl is registered to download with no authentication middleware
name is taken directly from the query string
file contents are written to the response

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check against root, no filepath.Rel check, no os.Root or fs.ValidPath use, no authentication or authorization. The avatar handler's filepath.Base call is not applied here. Also checked /avatar (files.go:22): Base() strips directory components, so it is not traversable.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param `f` straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no containment check, and files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd and is written out at files.go:18.

verdict_facts.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the query param `f` straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no containment check, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves to /etc/passwd and files.go:18 writes it to the response, and files.go:32 registers /dl with no auth.
